title: ci(site): deploy the docs from a GitHub Actions workflow every 6 hours, and turn Vercel's Git-triggered builds off (objectui#12178)
body:
Refs: #12178 · stacked on #12179

## Why

Almost all of the maintainer's Vercel bill was "Build CPU Minutes" for the `objectui` project (Root Directory `apps/site`, served at objectui.org). Vercel built once for every commit pushed to `main`, and started a preview build for every other branch (`claude/*`, `gh-readonly-queue/*`, `changeset-release/*`, ...) that the dashboard's Ignored Build Step then cancelled. Every production build since 2026-09-06 failed (#12178: 2023 failed production builds, about 9,400 build-minutes, the site frozen). This repository is public, so `ubuntu-latest` minutes are free. The maintainer decided that the docs deploy **only from `main`**, on **free compute**, **every 6 hours**.

## What

- **New `.github/workflows/docs-deploy.yml`**
  - Triggers: `schedule`, cron `43 5,11,17,23 * * *` (every 6 hours), and `workflow_dispatch`. Nothing else: no `push` trigger and no `paths` list.
  - Why that cron: `grep -rn 'cron:' .github/workflows/` shows hours 0/6/12/18, 1/7/13/19 and 2/8/14/20 each already carry another 6-hourly job. 5/11/17/23 meet only one daily patrol, at 05:23. Minute 43 is off the top of the hour and clear of the merge-queue patrol's :37 and :52. A comment in the file records this.
  - `concurrency: { group: docs-deploy-production, cancel-in-progress: true }`. A later run builds a tip that contains the earlier run's commits, so cancelling the earlier run loses nothing.
  - Steps, all run from the **repository root**: `vercel pull --yes --environment=production`, then `vercel build --prod`, then `vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod`, with the CLI pinned (`VERCEL_CLI_VERSION`, 60.1.3). The project's Root Directory is `apps/site`, so `vercel build` builds in `apps/site`, reads `apps/site/vercel.json` and writes `./.vercel/output`, and `vercel deploy --prebuilt` uploads that directory. I checked this against the pinned CLI's source: the build's work path is the cwd joined with the project's `rootDirectory`, and the prebuilt output dir is the cwd's `.vercel/output`. Running from inside `apps/site` would apply the Root Directory twice.
  - `VERCEL_ORG_ID` (`team_06nvlGKZCkwhzdXmRdxeCNnB`) and `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` (`prj_v1rXIczaI7YGmXmseQCLFUFOFxTB`) are inlined. They are identifiers, not secrets.
  - `VERCEL_TOKEN` is passed only to the `pull` and `deploy` steps. `vercel build` needs no token (it is in the CLI's no-token command list), and it runs `pnpm i` plus the whole workspace build, which includes every dependency's install scripts, so it never sees the token.
  - **Which way it fails:** the first step runs before checkout. If `VERCEL_TOKEN` is missing, it stops with `::error title=VERCEL_TOKEN is missing::...` and `exit 1`. If the ref is not `refs/heads/main`, it stops with `::error title=Docs deploy runs from main only::...`. A failed build or a failed upload is a red step. **Nothing turns into a skipped green.**
- **`apps/site/vercel.json`** gains `"git": { "deploymentEnabled": false }`. That is Vercel's documented switch for turning off Git-triggered deployments on every branch, and I validated the file against `https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json`. Once this is merged, Vercel builds nothing on push, and this workflow is the only way to production. The `installCommand` (`pnpm i`) and the fixed `buildCommand` come from #12179.
- **`content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`**: a `Docs Deploy (docs-deploy.yml)` section, a Workflow Inventory row and a `VERCEL_TOKEN` secrets row. **`scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`**: one declared entry. The section names `turbo run build`, which the job really runs but through `vercel build` and `vercel.json`, not in a `run:` step, so the command-parity sweep cannot see it.

## Secret: already in place

`VERCEL_TOKEN` exists as an **organization** secret of `objectstack-ai` (`gh api repos/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/organization-secrets` lists it, updated 2026-10-12T03:10:52Z), and this repository can see it. `secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN` resolves org secrets the same way, so nothing has to be configured before merging. The dry run below used it.

## Order with #12179

This branch contains #12179's commit. #12179 creates `apps/site/vercel.json`, and this PR adds the `git` block to it.

- If #12179 merges first (it can merge as soon as it is green), merge `origin/main` into this branch. The only conflict will be add/add on `apps/site/vercel.json`. Resolve it by taking **this branch's** version, which is #12179's file plus the `git` block.
- Alternatively, merge this PR alone (it carries #12179's change). #12179 is then redundant and can be shut without merging.

## Evidence

- **Build-only dry run of this exact workflow on GitHub Actions**: run 38200568488, success, 5m08s. It ran from a temporary commit that added a `pull_request` trigger and skipped the deploy step. That commit is reverted on this branch, and the final tree is byte-identical to the reviewed commit. In that run: `Vercel CLI 60.1.3 (Node.js 22.23.3)`, `vercel pull` downloaded the production settings into `./.vercel/project.json`, `vercel build` ran `Running "install" command: pnpm i` and `Running "cd ../.. && pnpm turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/site"`, turbo reported `Tasks: 30 successful, 30 total` (including `@object-ui/example-schema-catalog:build`, the package whose absence breaks the Vercel build in #12178), Next generated 559 of 559 static pages, then `Created all serverless functions`, then `Build Completed in .vercel/output`. `builds.json` shows `@vercel/next` with this file's `installCommand` and `buildCommand`.
- **Not yet exercised: the `vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod` upload.** The first real run after merge is that test.
- actionlint 1.7.12 reports nothing (shellcheck was not installed locally, so the `run:` scripts were not shell-linted). The YAML parses. A local run of the 88 `scripts/__tests__` files that read workflows or the CI/CD page passed, except one test whose timeout was not caused by this change: `check-i18n-dead-keys`, real-tree leg, 15 s, on a machine at load 4. CI is the judge.

## After merge

1. Publish once and verify: `gh workflow run docs-deploy.yml --repo objectstack-ai/objectui --ref main`, then watch the run. On green, the step summary prints the deployment URL, and objectui.org should show current content. #12179's build fix is part of this branch, so that run is expected to be green. If it is red, #12178 has the diagnosis of the build failure this replaces. The run is free either way.
2. From then on, the docs refresh **at most every 6 hours** (05:43, 11:43, 17:43 and 23:43 UTC). To publish immediately, use **Run workflow** on the workflow's Actions page (or the `gh workflow run` line above).
3. Shut #12178 by hand once a production deployment is READY. Neither PR carries a closing keyword.

Side effects worth knowing:
- The `Vercel` commit status stops appearing on PRs and commits once branches contain this `vercel.json`. `scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs` does not read statuses, so nothing waits on it.
- Branches created before this merge do not contain `git.deploymentEnabled: false`, so Vercel will still start a preview for them until they pick up `main`. The dashboard's Ignored Build Step still cancels those, so leave it in place for now.
- The dashboard build and install commands are overridden by `vercel.json` and no longer matter.
